title: feat(plugin-auth): a page navigation to the mobile hand-off that has to sign in first goes to the sign-in page
body:
Fixes #29997

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么**：手机 App 登录现在只需打开交接接口这一个地址。没登录、或会话超过 5 分钟的用户在系统浏览器里打开它，服务端直接跳到本部署的 Console 登录页，登录后回到交接接口，再把一次性令牌交回 App。App 自己的探测请求仍然拿到 401。
- **为什么改**：Google 这类不允许内嵌 WebView 的登录方式走这条流程，装好的 App 会用好几个月。原来 App 要自己知道 Console 登录页的路径和它怎么处理 `redirect`，Console 一升级改了其中一个，这些用户就卡在没有退路的页面上，App 也察觉不到。
- **风险与回滚**：旧版 App 不受影响，它现在的入口（直接打开 Console 登录页）照常可用。这是会话转移流程，但没有新增能力：令牌仍只发给 5 分钟内登录的会话，跨站打开和非法参数仍先回 400，不会跳到登录页；没挂 Console 的部署保持 401。回滚即还原本 PR。
- **先看**：`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/one-time-token-handoff.ts` 里的 `refusedSessionAnswer`（什么时候跳、什么时候还回 401）和 `resolveHandoffSignInEntry`（只取路径不换源、怎么判断有没有 Console）。
- **两分钟验证**：`pnpm --filter '@objectstack/plugin-auth^...' build && pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth exec vitest run src/one-time-token-handoff.test.ts`，预期 83 条全部通过。
- **需要你做的**：这是会话转移（auth）流程，请维护者审阅并合并本 PR。合并顺序见下面的 Landing order。

## What changes

`GET /api/v1/auth/one-time-token/handoff`, for a valid request whose session is missing or older than five minutes:

| Request | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| A page navigation | `302` to this deployment's Console sign-in page, with `redirect` naming the same request |
| Anything else (the app's probe included) | `401 UNAUTHENTICATED`, as before |
| A page navigation the sign-in page forwarded (`Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin`) | `401`, never another redirect |
| A page navigation on a deployment that does not serve the sign-in page | `401`, logged once at `warn` |

Nothing else moves. `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site` is still judged first, then the closed query set, the registered scheme and the challenge; an invalid request gets `400` and never reaches the sign-in page. A token is still minted only for a session under five minutes old (ruling A on #29714).

Spec: docblock only. Route ledger: the note. No schema, export or generated artefact moved.

## Design

**Telling a page navigation from an API call (constraint 1).** `Sec-Fetch-Dest` decides when a browser sends it: `document` is a navigation, and `empty` (a `fetch`) or `iframe` is not, whatever `Accept` says. With no Fetch Metadata, `Accept` naming `text/html` counts. A request with neither gets the `401`, which is what this route answered before. So the rule rests on no single header, and if a real system auth session turned out to send neither, the result is today's JSON rather than a wrong redirect.

NOT MEASURED: the headers a real `ASWebAuthenticationSession` or Custom Tabs sends. I cannot measure those here. Measured in headless Chromium 151 opening the route directly: `Sec-Fetch-Dest: document`, `Sec-Fetch-Site: none`, `Sec-Fetch-Mode: navigate`, an HTML `Accept`. The WebKit and Firefox builds Playwright has on this machine do not match its version, so they were not read either.

**Staying on the origin (constraint 3).** `AuthManager.getConsoleUrl` composes `${canonical origin}${uiBasePath}${path}` (confirmed in source), so using it as `Location` would move a browser that reached the deployment on another host. `Location` is root-relative and takes only the path of that URL, which keeps `uiBasePath` and any base path in `baseUrl` honoured without a second composer. The test sets `baseUrl: https://canonical.example.com` and `uiBasePath: /console/` and reads `/console/login?…` with no host.

**`redirect` (constraint 4)** is rebuilt from the validated parameters only: `redirect_uri`, `code_challenge`, and `code_challenge_method` if the request had it. The app's `redirect_uri` stays nested inside `redirect`, because `redirect_uri` at the top of the page's query, with `client_id`, is what the page reads as an OAuth authorize replay.

**No Console (constraint 6).** The route asks the composed server, in-process and per request, for the sign-in page, and redirects only when that answers `200` with an HTML document. `readShellConfig` and `anonymousFormDoorServes` in `packages/cli/src/utils/console.ts` already ask the composed app the same way. A route table would not do: `os serve` mounts a `503` responder on the same paths when the Console was not built. So these all keep the `401`: `--no-ui`, a Console not built, a host that redirects `/_console` to the control plane. So does a Console served by something in front of this process, which is the cost of asking in-process: that deployment stays on today's JSON.

**The loop (constraint 5) is real.** The session was really older than five minutes (the runs waited 5m10s) and the device clock was set 15 minutes behind, on this branch plus #29979's head and #30004's head:

| Tree | Hand-off requests | Where it ended |
| --- | --- | --- |
| This PR, the same-origin stop removed | **228 in 20 s, all `302`** | Still bouncing |
| This PR | 2: `302` (`none`), then `401` (`same-origin`) | JSON, after one bounce |
| This PR plus the page change below | 1: `302` (`none`) | The form; a sign-in on it ends in the `302` to the app |

Two parts stop it:

1. **On the route, here.** A navigation reporting `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin` that the route still refuses came from the sign-in page, so it gets the `401`. This is a narrow carve-out from "a page navigation gets the `302`", and it makes this PR safe in any landing order for a browser that sends that header. It also covers a session the page can see and the route cannot, such as a bearer session with no cookie.
2. **On the page, not here.** The redirect carries `handoff_refused_at`, the server's time of the refusal in epoch milliseconds.

### What #29979 still has to do

Not in this PR: that file belongs to #29979, and this PR does not touch `ui/apps/console/src/pages/auth/**`. In `isHandoffSessionFresh`, for a session that carries a `createdAt`, when the page's query has `handoff_refused_at` (digits only), the session is fresh only if `createdAt` is later than it:

```ts
if (refusedAt !== null) return createdAt > refusedAt;   // ahead of the five-minute check; two readings of the server's clock
```

Read the parameter from `window.location.search` inside `useHandoffRedirect`, so neither page changes. Everything else stays, including the branch for a session with no `createdAt`. This is 19 added lines and was measured in the third row above.

**Why a time and not the bare mark the #29979 thread agreed.** `SocialSignInButtons` defaults `callbackURL` to `window.location.href`, so a provider sign-in comes back to the same URL with the mark still on it. A bare mark would then hold the form over the brand-new session, which is a dead end for exactly the Google users this flow exists for. With a time, the new session's `createdAt` is later and the page forwards. It also spares a device whose clock is ahead, where a fresh provider session reads as too old today.

Until this lands, a browser that sends no Fetch Metadata can still bounce on a skewed clock (read from the code, not measured), so the app must not change its entry before it ships.

## Landing order and release

1. **Merge after #29979 and #30004**, or the nightly `live` tier goes red and files a card: the browser spec needs #29979's forward and #30004's `OS_TRUSTED_APP_SCHEMES`. This PR's own CI never collects the spec, so CI stays green either way.
2. **The page change above ships in the same release**, before the app changes its entry.
3. **Release.** This carries in the next release after it merges: 18.4.0 as pending changesets stand (six are `minor`, and these packages version together). objectstack-ai/mobile#190 can change its entry only once its server runs that release, because an older server answers the new entry with JSON.

## Tests

- `one-time-token-handoff.test.ts`: 83 tests on the real `AuthManager`, the real better-auth plugin and the real route registration. Page navigation with no session and with an old session gets the `302`; JSON, no headers, `*/*`, a `fetch` asking for HTML and an iframe get `401`; an unregistered scheme, a bad challenge, a plain method and an unknown parameter get `400` with no redirect; cross-site gets `400` first; the `redirect` it names signs in, comes back and redeems. `resolveHandoffSignInEntry` and `isPageNavigation` have their own tables.
- Pins: the two existing `401` pins send no navigation headers, so they stay and their titles now say so. No other pin of this route's `401` exists in the repo.
- `examples/app-showcase/e2e/mobile-signin-handoff.spec.ts`: signed out, open the hand-off, land on the form on this origin, sign in, see the `302` to the registered scheme, and redeem the token with the verifier (and fail without it).

## Acceptance notes

- **Where the browser test lives, and that it is nightly.** Not `ui/e2e`: `Live E2E UI` serves the Console from `vite preview` at the root and the backend there has no built Console to serve, so the route's redirect has nothing to land on. `examples/app-showcase/e2e` is the one lane where the backend serves the Console at its real mount. It runs in Nightly Tiers and a red night files a card, so a Console change that breaks this shows up the next night, not on that PR. The spec adds about a second of test time to that suite.
- **Scheme registration, against the dispatch's assumption.** A test-only stack config works only at the app root (the compile resolves connector spec paths from the config's directory) and through `composeStacks` (a spread loses the `defineStack` provenance, and `defineStack` on a built stack reports 71 cross-reference issues); I did not run it to the end after those two refusals. Every smoke spec would then boot a composed stack. `OS_TRUSTED_APP_SCHEMES` on the `webServer` is one line and the path a deployment uses, so the spec uses that and #30004 goes ahead of this PR.
- **File surface beyond the claim:** `examples/app-showcase/playwright.config.ts` (that one line) and the doc comment of `examples/app-showcase/test/showcase-smoke.live.test.ts`, which lists the suite's specs.
- **Cloud does not offer this flow.** On `objectstack-ai/cloud` main at `419ee51b`, the per-environment `AuthPlugin` has `registerRoutes: false` and nothing there mounts this route or sets `trustedAppSchemes`. Noted, not filed from here.
- `packages/qa/dogfood/test/principal-session-console-boot.dogfood.test.ts` skips on every CI run as far as the workflows read: none sets its Chromium path, and none builds the Console on that job. Noted, not filed.

## Verification

Head `fe2b8b4907`, merged with `origin/main` at `217ba78241`.

| eslint on the eight touched source files, `--no-inline-config` | exit 0, 0 errors, 0 warnings |
| `dispatch-gates --commands` (9 paths, 85 commands) | every one exit 0 |
| `dispatch-gates --ran` | `85 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 85 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED` |
| The five roster gates whose list lives under a touched directory (`check:meta-url-spelling`, `check:authz-resolver`, `check:changeset-fixed`, `check:error-code-casing`, `check:filter-alias-parity`) | exit 0 each |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated` | exit 0: all 14 generated artifacts up to date, so the docblock moved none |

The backend and the Console for the browser runs were built from a scratch tree: this branch merged with #29979's head `c6ac92e178` and #30004's head `3b20bb0151`, because the browser test needs both.

<summary>Browser spec and its ablations, on that scratch tree (Chromium 151, headless)</summary>

| Run | Result |
| --- | --- |

| Route's redirect removed, rebuilt, `ablation-dist-preflight` confirmed absent from `dist/` | red at `#login-email`: 25 s timeout on the JSON page |
| Page stops recognising the hand-off (`handoffNavigationTarget` returns null), Console rebuilt | red: 45 s timeout waiting for the `302` to the app, which is what a Console upgrade could do |

</details>

<summary>Unit ablations, through scripts/ablation-replace.mjs (each restored; blob equals HEAD)</summary>

| Mutation | Red |
| --- | --- |
| `isPageNavigation` guard deleted | 5: the JSON, no-header, wildcard, fetch and iframe pins |
| Same-origin stop deleted | 1 |
| The served check made `true` | 5: the four no-Console pins and the unserved pin |
| The `302` replaced by the refusal | 8 |
| `Location` given the full URL instead of the path | 6 |
| `handoff_refused_at` deleted | 2 |

</details>

**Declared narrowing — verification ran UNLOCKED.** `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh` could not take the shared verify lock on this host: no usable `flock`. The shared verify lock is declared Linux-only (`flock` is util-linux, and a stock macOS does not ship it), so the commands above were run directly, without the lock — a declared narrowing, not a silent one. No serialization guarantee held for these runs, nor for any sibling agent in this container while they ran.
